svg.text: Safety chain: original rover wiring + deadman and wireless E-stop in series with the rover E-stop
Numbers match the photo files in original_wiring_images/ where one exists (e.g. ③ = 3_e-stop_button_*). Dashed boxes repeat a component drawn in the other band.
A · Original wiring (before the Cube, deadman and wireless E-stop)
charged by ⑲, balanced by ⑥
dual channel, encoder A / B ports
48 V via ⑫a, 24 V via ⑫b
mixed mode: ch1 throttle, ch2 steer
drives blade ⑱ and generator ⑲
B · Additions: ㉓ and ㉔ in series with ③ on the 12 V and 24 V leads (nothing else added)
ch1 throttle, ch2 steer, ch8 mode
drop → 48 V + 24 V to ⑬ cut
㉓ module power: before its own contacts
power: electronics bus, not via ③
③/㉓ open → ⑮ off → RC failsafe
Nothing else is added: ③, ㉓ and ㉔ just break the 12 V and 24 V leads. The existing ⑫ relays stop the tracks and ⑯ stops the
engine and the blade on its shaft. Each of ㉓ and ㉔ needs 2 poles (DPST), one per lead.
• Series on both leads: ⑤ → ③ → ㉓ → ㉔ → 24 V to ⑫ coils and 12 V to ⑯. Any one opening stops all.
• Power taps: ㉓ module before its own contacts; ⑮ receiver + ㉔ module between ㉓ and ㉔.
If ㉔ cut its own receiver's power, the deadman could never close again.
• Cube ⑳ on the electronics bus: ③ / ㉓ open → ⑮ unpowered → RC failsafe → Hold.
• Blade is on the engine shaft: every stop also stops the engine. Restart it with ⑨.
• Receiver failsafe: no pulses (or ch5 = released), never hold-last.
• Unpowered tracks may freewheel on slopes: add spring-applied brakes if needed.
Verify on the rover before field use
• ㉓ / ㉔ relay contacts rated for the 12 V and 24 V lead currents
(⑫ coils, ⑯ engine controller, ⑮ receiver).
• ㉔ RC switch module turns its output OFF on signal loss (not hold-last).
• ⑯ stops the engine when its 12 V is removed (expected from the original wiring).
• Bench: after ③ / ㉓ reset, the Cube stays in Hold until the deadman is pressed.
• ④ breaker rating and which tap it protects.
dashed box = repeat of a component
